title: Sync Enriched Records to Salesforce with Cargo: Create, Update or Upsert
summary: Cargo's Salesforce connector creates, updates and upserts records natively. How to match accounts by record Id, then website, then name, fail on ambiguous matches instead of overwriting duplicates, and run the sync from the cargo-ai CLI.
body_markdown:
**Yes, Cargo writes enriched go-to-market records back to Salesforce natively:` upsertRecords` updates the records whose field matches your value and creates one when none does,` updateRecords` only updates, and` insertRecord` only creates.** To match by record Id, then website, then name without writing to duplicates, set` isFailingOnMultipleMatches: true` on the update or upsert: a row whose value matches more than one record fails, and nothing is overwritten. Website is the one key still checked with` countRecords` first, because the field holds URLs that an exact match misses.


Cargo platform data, 90 days to Oct 16 2026:` salesforce.updateRecords` ran 6.6M times across 37 workspaces.


## The three write actions#


All three take an` objectType` (` Account` here) and a list of` mappings` , each a Salesforce field API name and the value to write. Update and upsert also take one` matchingPropertyName` and one` matchingValue` , and find records with a SOQL query on` matchingPropertyName = matchingValue` .


Action No record matches One record matches Several records match


` insertRecord` Creates one Creates one more Creates one more


` updateRecords` Fails the row: “No records have been updated” Updates it Updates every match, or fails the row with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches`


` upsertRecords` Creates one, including the matched value Updates it Updates every match, or fails the row with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches`


Four details decide how you use them:


- **Several matches are all updated, unless you turn that off.** By default neither update nor upsert treats a duplicate as an error: if two accounts share a name, both get the write. The matches come from one page of SOQL results (up to 2,000 records) and are written in a single Salesforce update request, which accepts at most 200 records, so a value that matches more than 200 records fails the row instead of updating them. Set` isFailingOnMultipleMatches: true` and, when more than one record matches, the row fails with` 2 records match the matching value; "Fail on multiple matches" is on, so nothing was written` before anything is written. One match and no match behave as they do without it. The option is a boolean on` updateRecords` and` upsertRecords` , off by default; there is no mode that skips the row without failing it.
- **A stale Id fails the row.** An Id that no longer exists (the record was merged or deleted) fails that row with` No <object> record found with Id <id>` , in both` updateRecords` and` upsertRecords` . Upsert never creates a new record from an Id match.
- **A partial failure is not a failed row.** When several records match and some updates are rejected, the row succeeds and returns only the records that were updated. It fails only when none was.
- **` skipIfExist` protects what a rep typed.** Set it on a mapping and, on update, the field is written only when it is empty in Salesforce. On create, every mapping is written.


The connector also has` countRecords` , which returns` count` for a filter, and` matchRecord` , which returns the first matching record only. Use` countRecords` for the website check below: a first match cannot tell you there was a second.


## Match by record Id, then website, then name#


Use the strongest key each row has, and stop at the first one that gives an answer:


1. **Record Id (` Id` ).** If an earlier sync stored the Salesforce Id on your account, update by it. It is the only key that cannot be ambiguous.
2. **Website (` Website` ).** The Account` Website` field holds a URL as someone typed it (` https://www.acme.com` ,` acme.com/` ), not a bare domain, so an equality match on` acme.com` misses most of them. Count with the` contains` operator instead, then read the one match back with` matchRecord` to check its host really is your domain (` contains` also matches` acme.com.au` ), and update it by` Id` . If your org keeps a normalized domain in a custom field, match on that with equality instead.
3. **Name (` Name` ).** The weakest key, used only when the website matched nothing. Write by it with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches: true` : exactly one match is updated, more than one fails the row.


**Do not write ambiguous matches.** A row whose website count is more than 1 is not written, and a row whose name matches more than one account fails with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches: true` and writes nothing. Send both to a person instead: picking one of two duplicates by rule is how a sync writes enrichment onto the wrong account, and merging them is a separate decision. When no key matches anything, the upsert by` Name` creates the account; write its` Website` in the mappings so the next run finds it.


## Run it from the CLI#


Install the CLI, sign in, check the Salesforce connector, and find the actions. Each result carries the` action` object the commands below take:


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com
cargo-ai   connection   connector   list   --integration-slug   salesforce
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   list   upsert   --kind   connector   --integration-slug   salesforce


```


Every record you pass to` execute-batch` is the action’s input. Extra keys, like a` rowId` of your own, are carried through to the results file, which is how you join a count back to the account it belongs to.


**1. Accounts with a Salesforce Id: update by Id.**


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"salesforce","actionSlug":"updateRecords"}'   \
--records   '[{"objectType":"Account","matchingPropertyName":"Id","matchingValue":"001Hs00003XyZabIAF","mappings":[{"propertyName":"NumberOfEmployees","value":120},{"propertyName":"Description","value":"Payroll API for marketplaces","skipIfExist":true}]}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


**2. Accounts without an Id: count the matches by website.**


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"salesforce","actionSlug":"countRecords"}'   \
--records   '[{"rowId":"acc_1","objectType":"Account","filter":{"conjonction":"and","groups":[{"conjonction":"and","conditions":[{"propertyName":"Website","operator":"contains","values":["acme.com"]}]}]}}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


cargo-ai   orchestration   batch   download   --uuid   <  batch-uui  d  >


```


` batch download` returns a URL to a CSV: your input columns, including` rowId` , plus` cargo_count` . Note the spelling` conjonction` : it is the field name, and the filter is rejected without it.


**3. Write each row by what the count said.**


- ` cargo_count` is 1: run` matchRecord` with the same filter, check that` record.Website` is your domain, and run step 1’s command with` record.Id` as` matchingValue` .
- ` cargo_count` is more than 1: skip the row and list it for review.
- ` cargo_count` is 0: upsert by` Name` with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches: true` . One match is updated, several fail the row and write nothing, and none creates the account with its` Website` :


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"salesforce","actionSlug":"upsertRecords"}'   \
--records   '[{"rowId":"acc_1","objectType":"Account","matchingPropertyName":"Name","matchingValue":"Acme","isFailingOnMultipleMatches":true,"mappings":[{"propertyName":"Website","value":"https://acme.com"},{"propertyName":"NumberOfEmployees","value":120}]}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


The rows that matched several accounts are the failed runs of that batch: list them with` cargo-ai orchestration run list --batch-uuid <batch-uuid> --statuses error` , and` cargo-ai orchestration run get <run-uuid>` shows the error with the match count.


Pass` --limit 5` to any of these to run a pilot on the first five records and check the result in Salesforce before the full set.


## What each action returns#


- ` insertRecord` ,` updateRecords` and` upsertRecords` return` data` as an array of the Salesforce records they wrote, read back after the write with every field. A create returns one record; an update returns one per record it changed.
- ` countRecords` returns` count` , from a SOQL` COUNT()` query, so it is not capped at a page.
- ` matchRecord` returns` match` (true or false) and` record` , the first match or null.
- With` isFailingOnMultipleMatches: true` , an update or upsert that matched several records returns no data: the run fails with` <n> records match the matching value; "Fail on multiple matches" is on, so nothing was written` . Beyond 2,000 matches the number in that message is capped at one page; the row still fails.


None of the Salesforce actions carries a credit price.


## Contacts and leads work the same way#


The same actions take` "objectType":"Contact"` or` "objectType":"Lead"` . Match by` Id` first, then` Email` , with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches: true` so a value that matches twice fails instead of writing to both. To keep the sync running as accounts are enriched, put the same steps in a[play](https://www.getcargo.ai/product/plays) that fires when a record changes, rather than a script on a laptop. The HubSpot version of this page is[sync enriched accounts to HubSpot](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/sync-enriched-accounts-to-hubspot) , the broader rules for keeping the CRM clean are in[CRM hygiene as code](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/crm-hygiene-as-code) , and the[CRM enrichment cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/crm-enrichment) fills the identifiers this matching depends on.


## Frequently asked questions#


Yes. The Salesforce connector’s` upsertRecords` action queries for records whose field equals your value, updates every one it finds, and creates a record when it finds none.` updateRecords` only updates and` insertRecord` only creates.


By default,` updateRecords` and` upsertRecords` update both. Set` isFailingOnMultipleMatches: true` on the call and the row fails instead, with an error naming the match count, and neither account is written.


Not by equality on` Website` , because that field holds a URL rather than a bare domain. Count with the` contains` operator on` Website` , confirm the single match with` matchRecord` , and update it by` Id` ; or match on a custom field that stores the normalized domain.


Not with` updateRecords` : the update by Id fails that row, and no replacement is created.


Only if you let it. Set` skipIfExist` on a mapping and an update writes that field only when it is empty in Salesforce.
